summary: Master has made this moot. Full verify at batch 16/32 now runs on the head-paired path with scheduler_metadata=None, and so does full decode at batch > 1. The profile shows FA3 already runs prepare_varlen_num_blocks_kernel inside each of those calls, so a precomputed schedule only moves the same on-device scheduling kernel into a separate launch. The expected gain has no mechanism behind it.
justification: A: The premise is that without scheduler_metadata FA3 falls back to a static heuristic, and that a precomputed schedule balanced over the actual lengths would finish the longest tiles sooner. The current-best profile in FINDINGS contradicts this. Every full verify shape (verify_1 2.8 us, verify_16 3.2 us, verify_32 in the top-kernel lists) already runs flash::prepare_varlen_num_blocks_kernel<..., true>. That is the dynamic-split scheduler get_scheduler_metadata would launch, now running inside the FA3 call. LESSONS records the same thing: FA3 already sizes splits on the GPU under varlen. With metadata passed, FA3 skips its internal prepare kernel. It then uses the schedule from the same function, given the same inputs: cache_seqlens, and max_seqlen_k = page_table.shape[1]*page_size, which is also what FA3 derives internally for paged KV when none is given. So the schedule would match and the result would be flat or slightly slower: a separate launch, the Python wrapper and a metadata allocation, against a removed in-call launch of the same cost. The evidence offered was 'decode_16, which has the metadata, runs 201 us for the same bytes at q_len 1'. That is SGLang's number (201 vs 205 us), so it never isolated metadata. On master, full decode_16 also runs without metadata (paired, metadata=None) at 155.9 us against verify_16's 163.5 us. The gap is about 5%, explained by 8x the queries and causal masking, and the reference point the hypothesis relies on no longer exists. The geometry is also stale. The change says headdim=64 and num_heads_k=Hkv, but master's batch > 1 full path calls FA3 on a paired view (hdim 128, S = Hkv/2 KV heads, q padded to 128). A schedule built for the unpaired geometry would at best be ignored. At worst it mis-sizes the splits or tile counts for the actual call, which is a correctness risk. Master's own comment drops the judge's metadata for exactly this reason. verify_1 stays unpaired on master, but its expected direction is 'slower', so it cannot carry the result. Weakest link: the claim that the no-metadata path uses a static heuristic. The profile shows the dynamic scheduler running in-call.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: full verify_16/32 now goes through the paired view (hdim 128, Hkv/2 heads) with scheduler_metadata deliberately None. The spec's get_scheduler_metadata arguments (headdim=64, num_heads_k=Hkv) describe a geometry that no longer exists at batch > 1. Any result would mostly reflect a mismatch between the schedule and the call, not the effect of a balanced schedule.
paired-heads-launch-cleanup: it also changed what the decode_16 comparison point is. Full decode at batch > 1 now runs without metadata too, so 'decode has the metadata' is no longer true on master.
fused-preattention-triton: it touches neither the FA3 scheduling path nor the metadata, so it does not confound this change.
interference: C: No companion is warranted, because the parent result itself is moot. Correctly rebuilt for the paired geometry (headdim=128, num_heads_k=Hkv//2, num_heads=Hq), it would reproduce the schedule FA3 already computes in-call, so expect flat within the ~1.5-2.5% drift. An ab-revert of the pairing would test the change on a lineage that master no longer runs at these shapes, and could not change a decision. A control would have no sub-change to isolate: the change has only one, and the in-call prepare kernel already acts as that control. Spending a check here buys nothing, while the stronger levers for full verify (fa3-batched-q-verify, triton-flash-decode-full-verify) are queued.
rules_flags: Building the metadata from cache_seqlens inside kernel_fn on every call does not cache anything derived from inputs, and is allowed. max_seqlen_k must come from shapes (page_table.shape[1]*page_size), never cache_seqlens.max(), which would be a host sync. The spec already says so.
Not a rule break, but a correctness risk: passing a schedule whose geometry (num_heads_k, headdim) does not match the actual FA3 call can mis-size splits or tiles on the paired path.
open_questions: If anyone revives this, first confirm in sgl_kernel's flash_api that mha_fwd, given scheduler_metadata=None with varlen paged KV, calls prepare_varlen_num_blocks with the same num_splits heuristic and max_seqlen_k as get_scheduler_metadata would. The profile strongly suggests it does. Any remaining difference would be in pack_gqa or num_splits choices, which can be tested more cheaply as a num_splits/pack_gqa argument tweak, and the fa3-num-splits-* items were held for the same reason.
If it is kept for verify_1 only (unpaired), the hypothesis's own expectation there is 'slower', so it has no upside case.
